title.point: God wanted to live close to His people, so He gave Moses the plans for a house where He would dwell among them — and we want to be close to God too!

lastWeekReview.title: Moses—The Ten Commandments (2)
bullets: Last week we learned the LAST five commandments — all about how we treat other people.
6. Do not kill    7. Do not commit adultery    8. Do not steal
9. Do not give false testimony (no lying)    10. Do not covet (no jealousy)
God's laws are His words to us, showing how His people should live.
We keep them not just in big things, but in the small things too.
God wants us to DO His commandments — that's how we become His proper people!
lastWeekReview.discussion: Which of the last five commandments did you practice this week? Did you catch yourself before an unkind word, or choose to be thankful instead of jealous? Share your story!
lastWeekReview.verseQuote: "Therefore you shall keep My commandments and do them; I am Jehovah." — Leviticus 22:31

kidsContent.text: On the mountain, God gave Moses more than the Ten Commandments — He gave Moses the BLUEPRINTS for a house!
But this was no ordinary house. It was a place for God to meet with man and for man to meet with God. It was called the TABERNACLE.
Think about it: the God who had only been appearing to Moses now wanted to come CLOSE and dwell among ALL the children of Israel!
God spoke to Moses the plans for making Him a house where all His glory would come and He would live among His people.
🌟 God didn't want to be far away — He wanted to live right in the middle of the people He loves!

image.caption: The tabernacle — God's dwelling place among His people

kidsContent.text: God gave VERY specific instructions for every part of the tabernacle — because it was His house!

He named 12 materials in 3 groups: Minerals (gold, silver, bronze, onyx and precious stones), Plants (fine blue, purple, and scarlet linen, acacia wood, oil, spices), and Animals (goats' hair, rams' hide, porpoise skin).
He gave the exact pattern — every board, measurement, veil, and curtain. Nothing was random!
Inside were special furnishings: the ark of the testimony, the table of the bread of the presence, and the lampstand. God said how to make each one.
🌟 God was so careful because He loves us and wants to be close. Don't you want to be one who is always close to God?

lesson.practicePoint: This week, find a quiet moment each day to be CLOSE to God — talk to Him, thank Him, or sing to Him. He loves to be near you! Come share how it went.

memoryVerse.text: One thing I have asked from Jehovah, that I do seek: to dwell in the house of Jehovah all the days of my life.
memoryVerse.application: God built a house — the tabernacle — so He could live close to His people. And David's one desire was to be with God in His house always. God wants to be close to you — do you want to be close to Him?

parts.text: Materials: Cards for the 12 materials, three bins labeled MINERALS / PLANTS / ANIMALS, building blocks or craft sticks, a simple tabernacle 'blueprint' poster
Setup: Post the blueprint. Spread the 12 material cards on the floor.

Round 1 — Sort the Materials: Teams race to sort all 12 cards into the right bin — Minerals (gold, silver, bronze, onyx, precious stones), Plants (fine linen, acacia wood, oil, spices), Animals (goats' hair, rams' hide, porpoise skin).
Round 2 — Willing Hearts: Like the Israelites who gave willingly, each kid 'brings' a card to the tabernacle and names one thing THEY can give to God (time, singing, obedience, a kind word).
Round 3 — Furnish It: Match the furnishings — ark of the testimony, table of the bread, lampstand — to their spots on the blueprint.
📖 Connection: God was so specific because it was HIS house — He wanted everything ready so He could dwell close to His people!

rolePlayScript.text: Scene: Mount Sinai, in the cloud. God is speaking to Moses about a special building project.
After giving the Ten Commandments, God had one more wonderful thing to tell Moses — He wanted a house!
Let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell in their midst. I want to come close and live among My people.
You — the great God — want to live right here, among us? What should this house be like?
I will give you the exact plans: gold, silver, and bronze; fine blue, purple, and scarlet linen; acacia wood, oil, and spices. Every board and measurement, I will show you.
God was the best Architect! He designed every detail — the ark, the table of the bread, the lampstand — because it was His own dwelling place.
Moses comes down and tells the people.
People of Israel! God wants to live among us! Bring your gold, your linen, your best materials — whoever has a willing heart!
Here is my gold! I want to help build a house for God!
And here is fine linen and acacia wood! Imagine — God Himself, living right in the middle of our camp!
God doesn't want to be far away — He wants to dwell with us, and we want to be close to Him!

description.text: Setup: Two teams. At the far end, place a pile of 'materials' (bean bags, foam blocks, or soft bricks) and a marked 'building spot.'
Rules: One runner at a time carries ONE material down and carefully stacks it at the building spot, then runs back to tag the next runner.
Goal: Build the tallest standing 'tabernacle' before time runs out — teamwork and care count (just like God's careful plans)!
Twist: Drop your material on the way? Go back and pick it up — God's people bring their gifts carefully!
📖 Connection: The whole camp worked together to build God's house — we can serve God together too!
Materials: Bean bags/foam blocks, cones, timer
Setup: Label three corners of the gym MINERALS, PLANTS, and ANIMALS.
Rules: The leader shouts a tabernacle material (e.g. 'GOLD!', 'LINEN!', 'GOATS' HAIR!') and kids race to the correct corner.
Out: Last one to the right corner (or anyone in the wrong corner) does 5 jumping jacks and jumps back in.
Speed Round: Call materials faster and faster — see who really knows the 12 materials!
📖 Connection: God used minerals, plants, and animals to build His house — every good thing comes from Him!
Materials: Three corner signs, list of the 12 materials

description.text: Give teams sheets/blankets, rope, and cones or poles to build their own 'tabernacle' tent in a marked area.
Challenge: Follow a simple 'blueprint' card exactly — a doorway facing one way, a courtyard 'fence' around it — just like God's specific plans.
Once built, each team sits inside and shares one way they can stay close to God this week.
Twist: A 'material hunt' first — find hidden cards (gold, linen, wood) before you may start building!
Materials: Sheets/blankets, rope, cones or poles, blueprint cards, hidden material cards

outdoor.tip: ⛺ The tabernacle shows how much God wants to be close to us. Help kids feel that God isn't far away — He longs to dwell with His people, and we can draw near to Him every day.
